briefs.rationale: The rewritten brief keeps the ordinal, combinatorial, descriptive-set-theoretic, proof-theoretic, PCF, reflection, Boolean-algebra and large-cardinal strands, including the inner-model and condensation results, and covers the four gained pages: closure, distributivity and chain conditions with nice-name counting controlling the continuum under Cohen, collapse and Lévy-collapse forcing; the choice-failure models — Dedekind-finite sets of reals in Cohen's first symmetric model, non-well-orderable atoms and countable pairs in the Fraenkel--Mostowski, second Fraenkel and ordered Mostowski permutation models, with the ZFA countable-pairs result transferred to ZF by Jech--Sochor; and finite-support iterations preserving the ccc to force Martin's Axiom with failure of CH.

The rewritten brief keeps the normed-space, Baire-category, Fourier, Hahn--Banach, distribution and duality spine with its DC and AC-omega boundaries, and covers the three gained pages: tempered distributions on Schwartz space via the finite-seminorm criterion, with weak and strong dual topologies and the 2pi-normalized Fourier automorphism; Banach--Alaoglu from the product embedding and ultrafilter lemma, Goldstine, weak-star metrizability and the Krein--Milman, Bauer and Milman convex geometry with their AC costs stated; and reflexivity as weak compactness of the unit ball, with Lp reflexivity, Eberlein--Smulian, Schur's property, uniform convexity, James and Bishop--Phelps. The existing locally-convex and continuous-separation close of the track is retained.

The rewritten brief keeps the measure, integration, Lp, representation, differentiation and interpolation strands with their choice and sigma-finiteness hypotheses, and closes the dynamical strand with the gained ergodic-theorems page: the maximal ergodic inequality giving Birkhoff's almost-everywhere theorem for L1 observables on sigma-finite spaces, von Neumann's L2 mean theorem with the limit identified on the invariant sigma-algebra, unique ergodicity via uniform averages of continuous functions, and the Weyl equidistribution, Borel normality and fair-coin strong-law applications.
